latestHairCandidateStatus: r247 keeps the selected r244 physical hair response and r245 5mm localized back-seam closure, bakes all visible main/overlay/root-veil curves to writable geometry, and projects them to two-frame body clearance. The complete frame 1/20 audit passes with zero hair/body/clothing violations. Eleven-view review still rejects promotion: the middle part continues too far toward the nape, the front hairline is hard, and the bob ends remain too blunt. It is the newest collision-safe legacy-body hair technical candidate; website v83 is unchanged.
latestHairMaterialStudy: r192 Aevrynd-owned satin EEVEE branch derived from the offline CC0 r129 node group; geometry parity and 11-shot visual review passed; strict hero-hair gate remains open
latestHairPerformanceResearch: r227-r229 layer isolation, deterministic density pruning and exact runtime trajectory subsetting
latestHairPerformanceResearchStatus: r227 proves the 11,193-curve main follow layer, rather than the 30 flyaways, causes most thin crossing noise. r228 selects a 55.9% deterministic subset for technical validation. r229 preserves original curve indices, reduces authored main points from 211,265 to 117,868 and runtime follow bytes by 44.28%, passes the full frame 1/20 collision audit and five dynamic states with zero violations, and preserves visible motion continuity. The 11-shot top view fails hero quality because the broad scalp proxy and intersecting thin strands remain visible, so r192 stays the hair candidate and r229 is only a reusable performance branch.
latestEyeCandidateStatus: r210 inherits r200 mouth placement, r192 hair and r175 owned iris/cornea materials, then raises only the evaluated upper eyelid field by up to 1.481mm. Upper lashes follow by up to 1.701mm with 0.45mm outward clearance; lower lids, tear menisci and caruncles stay at their proven r200 positions. An iterative topology guard restores 33 body vertices across 14 contacted faces and converges both tear menisci to zero body overlaps at frames 1 and 20. The full collision audit reports no regressions across all eye and mouth layers, mouth pair contacts, body self-intersection, hair/body/clothing penetration, or nonfinite shape-key points. The complete 11-shot review shows a more awake aperture without visible guard dents or pose breakage. Strict eye quality is about 52/100; eyelid thickness, crease anatomy and lash clustering remain below hero quality.
latestFaceCandidateStatus: r210 builds on collision-safe r200 and selects the r205 d-open upper-lid-only field. It moves 2,388 evaluated body vertices before collision guards, preserves the lower-lid/tear assembly, and uses iterative frame 1/20 BVH feedback to restore only 33 guard vertices until tear contacts reach zero. The full audit has zero regressions and the 11-shot review remains stable in neutral and posed views. The face reads less half-closed at normal distance; strict face quality rises from about 47/100 to about 49/100. Orbital volume, brows/lashes, nasal and perioral planes, skin response and hairline still fail modern hero-character quality. It remains a technical candidate and website v83 is unchanged.
latestSkinCandidateStatus: r173 recomputes owned complexion and roughness fields on the actual 41,692-vertex v249 body, adding cheek/nose/under-eye/temple color zones, T-zone and dry-zone roughness, and dual-scale pores. r175 combines that skin with the owned iris and physical cornea response. Full 11-shot review passes and the frame 1/20 geometry SHA-256 is exactly identical to r163 across 61 objects/1,454,277 points, proving materials changed without collision geometry changes. Strict skin material quality is about 55/100; face geometry remains about 42/100, so it is not a final visual promotion.
latestRejectedExperiment: r202 full eye-assembly opening, r204 shared clearance, r206/r207/r209 fixed-mask upper-lid repairs
latestRejectedReason: r202 c-open improved the aperture but moving lower lid, tear film and caruncle together created accessory collisions. r204 showed a shared outward offset can clear lashes but worsens tear-film contact. r206 left lash and right tear regressions; r207 and r209 moved the collision to neighboring tear faces. r210 replaced fixed guards with iterative frame 1/20 topology convergence and passed.
latestBrowResearch: r211-r216 component inspection, layer isolation, root-order rejection, surface sampling and authored anatomical direction-field sweeps
latestBrowResearchStatus: No r211-r216 experiment passes the strict normal-distance gain gate. Existing r210 density supplies the arch but is flat close; original fibers are sparse and regular. Root-order rotation creates curls/spikes, duplicates are negligible, surface sampling reads as parallel brush hair, and short authored micro-fill disappears at normal distance. No blend candidate was promoted.
latestFaceMaterialResearch: r217-r219 nasal/perioral displacement and skin optical-response sweeps
latestFaceMaterialResearchStatus: r217 moves up to 4,695 evaluated vertices with 1.156mm maximum displacement but independent lip/nostril layers and the current skin response suppress the intended planes; stronger motion would raise collision risk. r219 makes pores more visible by lowering roughness and raising specular/SSS/coat, but all variants become oily or plastic. Both studies are rejected and r210 remains the face candidate.
latestMouthResearch: r220-r226 authored-state isolation, integrated lip volume/color, anatomical vermilion masking and local retopology studies
latestMouthResearchStatus: r220 confirms that r210 already hides the legacy Lip_Upper, Lip_Lower and Mouth_WetLine shells, so the formal mouth is the continuous 41,692-vertex body surface. r221-r223 show that simple displacement and color cannot resolve the flat upper vermilion. r224 exposes triangle-shaped POINT-color interpolation boundaries. r225 produces a swollen ridge instead of a natural lip plane. r226 proves local subdivision can add 5,805 vertices while preserving all 21 armature groups and zero unweighted points, but its rectangular boundary creates visible commissure and nasolabial shading dents. All variants are rejected and r210 remains the face candidate.

latestHairScalpCandidateStatus: r163 derives a clean scalp shell from the same shaped body surface, copies all 21 skin-weight groups and Armature deformation, excludes the concave temple crease, and keeps 1.2mm authored clearance. Its 2,626 vertices/2,438 faces and r162 177,353-point pruned curly layer pass frame 1/20 collision checks against body and all three clothing solids. It reduces crown exposure but still fails strict overall hair appearance, so it is a scalp deformation/collision technical candidate only.
latestFoundationCandidateStatus: r249 replaces the structurally limited legacy body experiment with the official Blender Human Base Meshes 1.4.1 realistic female CC0 source, recorded by official URL and SHA-256. Its continuous 10,582-vertex body has materially better eye sockets, nose, lips, ears, jaw, hands, knees and whole-body proportions. r250 transfers all 21 Aevrynd rig groups by nearest-surface interpolation; r251 normalizes 1,000 over-summed vertices. The evaluated frame 1/20 deformation audit passes over 169,362 vertices and 338,720 edges: zero nonfinite points, stable topology, volume ratio 1.01577, edge ratios 0.546-1.975, and zero severe edges. It remains a foundation candidate because clothing, hair, cornea, tear film, brows/lashes, facial identity sculpt and runtime export are pending.
latestFoundationLicense: CC0-1.0; Blender Studio and community contributors; source manifest blender-human-base-meshes-v141.source.json; no runtime Blender, MetaHuman, Unreal Engine, subscription or platform dependency.
latestFaceResearch: r248 procedural facial-plane sweep and r249-r251 CC0 foundation replacement
latestFaceResearchStatus: r248 moves more than 10,000 legacy-body vertices by up to 2.422mm but produces only marginal visible improvement and buries separate brow shells, proving the legacy topology/layer stack is the bottleneck. r249-r251 establish and rig a better CC0 foundation. The new base clearly improves primary facial anatomy, but current procedural skin is striped/overlit and the simple iris discs lack cornea, tear, lid-margin, brow and lash layers, so it is not yet presentation-ready.
